title: Predict next year's copper price to the dollar
summary: An exact copper-price forecast would invent precision; use a conditional cost range.

blocks.heading: Next year’s copper price is unknown
blocks.body: A forecast to the dollar would imply more knowledge than the evidence provides. Define the market, currency, unit and date first: a yearly average in USD per metric tonne is a different question from a spot quote on December 31.

blocks.heading: A purchasing stress test, not a price prediction
blocks.caption: The $10,000 baseline and ±20% moves are invented arithmetic inputs. They are not today’s price, a forecast interval or assigned probabilities.

blocks.heading: Ask the question a buyer can act on
blocks.body: Can the job absorb a $4,000 change in this material line? If not, compare a time-limited supplier quote, an escalation clause and a smaller staged order. Their actual costs and terms need quotes; this example does not recommend a financial trade.

blocks.heading: What would narrow the uncertainty?
blocks.body: A dated supplier quote establishes a purchasable price for specified terms. Inventory, demand, supply disruptions and exchange rates can help explain market changes, but they do not turn a next-year estimate into a guaranteed number.
